items.explain: $V=2\pi\int_0^4x\left(\frac{x+4}{2}-x\right)dx=\pi\int_0^4(4x-x^2)dx=\frac{32\pi}{3}$.

items.q: Revolve the triangle bounded by $2y=x+4$, $y=x$ and $x=0$ about the line $x=4$ (shell method). Volume:
items.explain: Radius $4-x$, height $\frac{x+4}2-x=\frac{4-x}{2}$: $V=\pi\int_0^4(4-x)^2dx=\frac{64\pi}{3}$ (see the note on the Sources page about the printed key).

items.q: Revolve the triangle bounded by $2y=x+4$, $y=x$ and $x=0$ about the line $y=8$ (washer method). Volume:
items.explain: Outer radius $8-x$, inner radius $8-\frac{x+4}2$: $V=\pi\int_0^4\left[(8-x)^2-\left(\frac{12-x}{2}\right)^2\right]dx=48\pi$.

items.q: Revolve the region between $y=4-x^2$ and $y=2-x$ about the $x$-axis. Volume:
items.explain: They meet where $4-x^2=2-x$: $x=-1,2$. Washers: $\pi\int_{-1}^2\left[(4-x^2)^2-(2-x)^2\right]dx=\frac{108\pi}{5}$.

items.q: The region in the first quadrant under $y=x^2$ and left of $x=1$ is revolved about the line $x=-1$. Volume:
items.explain: Shells of radius $x+1$ and height $x^2$: $V=2\pi\int_0^1(x+1)x^2dx=2\pi\left(\frac14+\frac13\right)=\frac{7\pi}6$.

items.q: Find the length of $y=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+\dfrac{1}{4x}$ for $1\le x\le3$.
items.explain: $y'=x^2-\frac1{4x^2}$ and $1+y'^2=\left(x^2+\frac1{4x^2}\right)^2$, so $L=\int_1^3\left(x^2+\frac1{4x^2}\right)dx=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}-\frac1{4x}\right]_1^3=\frac{53}6$.
By symmetry $L=8\int_{\sqrt2/4}^1\sqrt{1+y'^2}\,dx$ with $y=(1-x^{2/3})^{3/2}$ (and $\sqrt{1+y'^2}=x^{-1/3}$): the integral evaluates to $6$.

items.q: Perpendicular segments of length $h=y$ are erected at the points of $y=2\sqrt x$, $0\le x\le3$. The area of the surface so formed ($\int y\,ds$) is
items.explain: $ds=\sqrt{1+\frac1x}\,dx$, $y=2\sqrt x$: $\int_0^32\sqrt x\sqrt{1+\frac1x}\,dx=2\int_0^3\sqrt{x+1}\,dx=\frac43\left(4^{3/2}-1\right)=\frac{28}{3}$.

items.q: On a circle of radius $a$, vertical segments of length $ks$ are drawn at arc length $s$ from $(a,0)$ once around. The area of the surface is
items.explain: $s=a\theta$, $ds=a\,d\theta$: area $=\int_0^{2\pi}k(a\theta)(a\,d\theta)=ka^2\cdot\frac{(2\pi)^2}{2}=2\pi^2ka^2$.

items.q: Length of the curve $y^2+2y=2x+1$ from $(-1,-1)$ to $(7,3)$ (set up with $x=\frac{y^2+2y-1}{2}$): $L=\int_{-1}^{3}\sqrt{1+(y+1)^2}\,dy\approx$
items.explain: $\frac{dx}{dy}=y+1$, so $L=\int_{-1}^3\sqrt{1+(y+1)^2}\,dy\approx9.294$ (numerical integration; the printed key says $\approx9.29$).
$y'=\tan x$, so $\sqrt{1+y'^2}=\sec x$ and $L=\int_0^{\pi/6}\sec x\,dx=\ln|\sec x+\tan x|\,\Big|_0^{\pi/6}=\ln\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt3}+\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)=\ln\sqrt3$.

Evaluate any antiderivative at the endpoints.
$u=-\cot z$, $du=\csc^2z\,dz$: $\int e^u\,du=e^u$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $e^{- \frac{\cos{\left(z \right)}}{\sin{\left(z \right)}}}+C$.
Complete the square: $2\theta-\theta^2=1-(\theta-1)^2$; with $u=\theta-1$ the integral is $\arcsin u$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\arcsin{\left(\theta - 1 \right)}+C$.
$u=2\ln x$, $du=\frac{2}{x}dx$: $\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}=\arcsin u$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\arcsin{\left(2 \ln{\left(x \right)} \right)}+C$.
$u=e^z$, $du=e^zdz$: $e^{z+e^z}dz=e^u\,du$, so the antiderivative is $e^{u}=e^{e^z}$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $e^{e^{z}}+C$.
Parts twice with $u=$ the polynomial: $e^r(P-P'+P'')$ with $P=r^2+r+1$: $e^r\left(r^2+r+1-(2r+1)+2\right)$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\left(r^{2} - r + 2\right) e^{r}+C$.

Parts twice returns the original integral: $I=e^\theta(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)-I$, so $I=\frac12e^\theta(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{\left(\sin{\left(\theta \right)} - \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\right) e^{\theta}}{2}+C$.
No parts needed: $u=\sqrt x$, $du=\frac{dx}{2\sqrt x}$ gives $2\int e^udu$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $2 e^{\sqrt{x}}+C$.

Integrate by parts three times (tabular method): $x^3\cdot\frac{\sin2x}2+3x^2\frac{\cos2x}{4}-6x\frac{\sin2x}{8}-6\frac{\cos2x}{16}$ evaluated from $0$ to $\frac\pi2$; the value is $\frac{3}{4} - \frac{3 \pi^{2}}{16}\approx-1.1006$.
Parts: $u=x$, $dv=\cos x\,dx$: $x\sin x-\int\sin x\,dx$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $x \sin{\left(x \right)} + \cos{\left(x \right)}+C$.
Parts twice (or $e^x(P-P'+P'')$ with $P=x^2$). Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\left(x^{2} - 2 x + 2\right) e^{x}+C$.
Parts twice and solve for the integral: $I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)-I$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{\left(\sin{\left(x \right)} + \cos{\left(x \right)}\right) e^{x}}{2}+C$.

Odd power: save one $\cos x$, write $\cos^4x=(1-\sin^2x)^2$, put $u=\sin x$: $\int(1-2u^2+u^4)du$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{\sin^{5}{\left(x \right)}}{5} - \frac{2 \sin^{3}{\left(x \right)}}{3} + \sin{\left(x \right)}+C$.
$\tan^4x=\tan^2x(\sec^2x-1)=\tan^2x\sec^2x-\sec^2x+1$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $x + \frac{\tan^{3}{\left(x \right)}}{3} - \tan{\left(x \right)}+C$.
$\frac{x^2}{x^2+1}=1-\frac{1}{x^2+1}$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $x - \arctan{\left(x \right)}+C$.
$u=\sqrt x$, $dx=2u\,du$: $\int\frac{2u\,du}{u^2-u}=2\int\frac{du}{u-1}=2\ln|u-1|$ (for $x>1$). Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $2 \ln{\left(\sqrt{x} - 1 \right)}+C$.

$2^{\ln z^3}=e^{3\ln2\cdot\ln z}$; with $u=\ln z$, $du=\frac{dz}z$: $\frac1{16}\int2^{3u}du=\frac{2^{3u}}{16\cdot3\ln2}$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{2^{\ln{\left(z^{3} \right)}}}{48 \ln{\left(2 \right)}}+C$.
$u=\tan x$, $du=\sec^2x\,dx$: $\int\frac{du}{u}=\ln u$; $\ln\tan\frac\pi3-\ln\tan\frac\pi4=\ln\sqrt3=\frac12\ln3$. Value: $\frac{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2}$.
$1+\cos4x=2\cos^22x$, so $\sqrt{\cdot}=\sqrt2\cos2x$ on $[0,\frac\pi4]$: $\sqrt2\left[\frac{\sin2x}{2}\right]_0^{\pi/4}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$. Value: $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
$u=\cos2\theta$, $du=-2\sin2\theta\,d\theta$: $-4\int u^3du=-u^4$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $- \cos^{4}{\left(2 \theta \right)}+C$.
$\sqrt{1-\cos^2\theta}=|\sin\theta|=\sin\theta$ on $[0,\pi]$: $[-\cos\theta]_0^\pi=2$ (a common slip is to write $\sqrt{\sin^2\theta}=\sin\theta$ on intervals where $\sin<0$). Value: $2$.
$u=\tan x$, $du=\sec^2x\,dx$: $\int u^2du$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{\tan^{3}{\left(x \right)}}{3}+C$.
Product-to-sum: $\cos3x\cos4x=\frac12[\cos x+\cos7x]$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{\sin{\left(x \right)}}{2} + \frac{\sin{\left(7 x \right)}}{14}+C$.

$\frac{\sec^3x}{\tan x}=\frac{\sec x(1+\tan^2x)}{\tan x}=\csc x+\sec x\tan x$; integrate each: $-\ln|\csc x+\cot x|+\sec x$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $- \ln{\left(\cot{\left(x \right)} + \csc{\left(x \right)} \right)} + \sec{\left(x \right)}+C$.

Half-angle: $\sin^2x=\frac{1-\cos2x}{2}$, then parts on $\int x\cos2x$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{x^{2}}{4} - \frac{x \sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{4} - \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{8}+C$.
$x=3\sin\theta$: $\int d\theta=\theta=\arcsin\frac x3$; at $x=\frac32$: $\arcsin\frac12=\frac\pi6$. Value: $\frac{\pi}{6}$.

$3t=\sin\theta$: $\frac13\int\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac16(\theta+\sin\theta\cos\theta)$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{t \sqrt{1 - 9 t^{2}}}{2} + \frac{\arcsin{\left(3 t \right)}}{6}+C$.

Multiply by $\sqrt{x+1}/\sqrt{x+1}$: $\frac{x+1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$; split into $\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}+\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $- \sqrt{1 - x^{2}} + \arcsin{\left(x \right)}+C$.

$v=\sin\theta$: $\int\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^4\theta}d\theta=\int\tan^2\theta\sec^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac{\tan^3\theta}3$, and $\tan\theta=\frac{v}{\sqrt{1-v^2}}$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{v^{3}}{3 \left(1 - v^{2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}+C$.

Three methods agree. $u$-substitution: $u=1-x^2$, $x^3dx=-\frac12(1-u)\,du$, giving $-\frac12\int(1-u)\sqrt u\,du=-\frac13u^{3/2}+\frac15u^{5/2}$. (Parts: $\int x^2\cdot x\sqrt{1-x^2}dx$; trig sub: $x=\sin\theta$.) Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)^{\frac{5}{2}}}{5} - \frac{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}+C$.

$x=2\tan\theta$: $\int\sec\theta\,d\theta=\ln|\sec\theta+\tan\theta|=\ln\left|\frac{\sqrt{4+x^2}+x}{2}\right|$ (the constant $\ln\frac12$ is absorbed in $C$). Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\ln{\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 4} \right)}+C$.

$5x=2\sec\theta$: $\frac15\int\sec\theta\,d\theta=\frac15\ln|\sec\theta+\tan\theta|=\frac15\ln\left|\frac{5x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{25x^2-4}}{2}\right|$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{\ln{\left(5 x + \sqrt{25 x^{2} - 4} \right)}}{5}+C$.
Improper (degrees equal): divide first, $\frac{t^2+8}{t^2+5t+6}=1+\frac{2-5t}{(t+2)(t+3)}$, then $\frac{2-5t}{(t+2)(t+3)}=\frac{A}{t+2}+\frac{B}{t+3}$ with $A=12$, $B=-17$.

Cover-up: $A=\frac{1+4+1}{2\cdot4}=\frac34$, $B=\frac{1-4+1}{(-2)(2)}=\frac12$, $C=\frac{9-12+1}{(-4)(-2)}=-\frac14$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{3 \ln{\left(x - 1 \right)}}{4} + \frac{\ln{\left(x + 1 \right)}}{2} - \frac{\ln{\left(x + 3 \right)}}{4}+C$.
Long division: $\frac{2x^3-2x^2+1}{x^2-x}=2x+\frac{1}{x(x-1)}=2x+\frac1{x-1}-\frac1x$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $x^{2} - \ln{\left(x \right)} + \ln{\left(x - 1 \right)}+C$.

$t^3+t^2-2t=t(t-1)(t+2)$. Cover-up: $A_0=\frac{1}{(-1)(2)}=-\frac12$, $A_1=\frac{1}{1\cdot3}=\frac13$, $A_{-2}=\frac{1}{(-2)(-3)}=\frac16$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $- \frac{\ln{\left(t \right)}}{2} + \frac{\ln{\left(t - 1 \right)}}{3} + \frac{\ln{\left(t + 2 \right)}}{6}+C$.

Integrating term by term: $\arctan s+\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{1}{(s-1)^2}$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\arctan{\left(s \right)} + \frac{1}{s - 1} - \frac{1}{\left(s - 1\right)^{2}}+C$.

items.q: Evaluate $L=\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{n}\ln\sqrt[n]{1+\tfrac kn}$ by recognising a Riemann sum.
items.explain: $\ln\sqrt[n]{1+\frac kn}=\frac1n\ln\left(1+\frac kn\right)$, so $L=\int_0^1\ln(1+x)\,dx=[(1+x)\ln(1+x)-x]_0^1=2\ln2-1$.

With $x-3=2\tan\theta$: $\int\frac{2\sec^2\theta\,d\theta}{16\sec^4\theta}=\frac18\int\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac1{16}(\theta+\sin\theta\cos\theta)$, and $\sin\theta\cos\theta=\frac{\tan\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}=\frac{2(x-3)}{x^2-6x+13}$. Check: differentiating gives the integrand. Answer: $\frac{2 x - 6}{16 \left(x^{2} - 6 x + 13\right)} + \frac{\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{3}{2} \right)}}{16}+C$.

items.q: The arc $y=\frac13\sqrt x\,(3-x)$, $0\le x\le3$, is rotated about the $x$-axis. The surface area is

items.q: For which $k$ does $\displaystyle\int_2^\infty\dfrac{dx}{x\ln^kx}$ converge, and what is its value then?
items.explain: $u=\ln x$: $\int_{\ln2}^\infty u^{-k}du=\left[\frac{u^{1-k}}{1-k}\right]_{\ln2}^\infty$, which is finite iff $k>1$ and then equals $\frac{(\ln2)^{1-k}}{k-1}$. For $k=1$ it is $\ln\ln x\to\infty$.
For $p\ne1$, $\left[\frac{x^{1-p}}{1-p}\right]_1^\infty$ is finite only when $p>1$; for $p=1$ it is $\ln x\to\infty$.
Near $0$ the integrand blows up unless $p<1$.

Divide by $(11/12)^n$: the numerator is $\left(\frac{120}{121}\right)^n\to0$ and the denominator tends to $1$; the limit is $0$. Result: $0$.

items.q: Let $a_1=-1$, $a_{n+1}=\dfrac{a_n+6}{a_n+2}$ and assume $(a_n)$ converges. Its limit is

If $a_n\to L$: $L=2+\frac1L\Rightarrow L^2-2L-1=0\Rightarrow L=1\pm\sqrt2$; all terms are positive, so $L=1+\sqrt2$.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\cos\dfrac{n\pi}{2}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: $a_n=\cos\frac{n\pi}2$ takes the values $1,0,-1,0,\dots$ and does not tend to $0$: the $n$-th term test shows divergence.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{n^n}{n!}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: $\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=\left(1+\frac1n\right)^n\to e>1$ (ratio test), so $a_n\to\infty$.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}ne^{-n^2}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: Integral test: $\int_1^\infty xe^{-x^2}dx=\frac1{2e}<\infty$ ($f$ is positive and decreasing for $x\ge1$).

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{2^{\ln n}}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: $2^{-\ln n}=n^{-\ln2}$ is a $p$-series with $p=\ln2\approx0.69<1$: diverges (equivalently $\int_1^\infty x^{-\ln2}dx=\infty$).

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{\cos^2n}{n^{3/2}}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: $0\le\frac{\cos^2n}{n^{3/2}}\le\frac{1}{n^{3/2}}$, a convergent $p$-series ($p=\frac32>1$): comparison test.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{5^n}{\sqrt{n\,4^n}}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: $a_n=\frac{(5/2)^n}{\sqrt n}\to\infty$ (exponential beats $\sqrt n$), so the series diverges by the $n$-th term test (the Limit Comparison Test with $(5/2)^n$ also fails to give convergence).

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{n!}{10^n}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: Ratio test: $\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=\frac{n+1}{10}\to\infty>1$.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{n^n}{(2^n)^2}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: Root test: $\sqrt[n]{a_n}=\frac{n}{4}\to\infty>1$.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{\sqrt n+1}{\sqrt{n^2+3}}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: Compare with $\frac1{\sqrt n}$: $\frac{\sqrt n+1}{\sqrt{n^2+3}}\ge\frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt{n^2+3n^2}}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt n}$, a divergent $p$-series ($p=\frac12$).

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt n\,\ln n}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: For large $n$, $\ln n<n^{1/4}$, so $\frac{1}{\sqrt n\ln n}>\frac{1}{n^{3/4}}$ (divergent $p$-series, $p=\frac34$).

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{n^{\sqrt2}}{2^n}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: Ratio test: $\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=\frac12\left(1+\frac1n\right)^{\sqrt2}\to\frac12<1$.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{2^n}{3^n}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: Geometric series with ratio $\frac23$, $|r|<1$.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{n\ln^2n}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: Integral test: $\int_2^\infty\frac{dx}{x\ln^2x}=\frac1{\ln2}<\infty$.

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{n^{1.01}}$ converge or diverge?
opts: the test is inconclusive; no conclusion can be drawn
items.explain: $p$-series with $p=1.01>1$ converges (very slowly).

items.q: Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ converge or diverge?
